subject: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit onboarding and pen-test scoping
messages:
From: Marta Diaz <marta.diaz@acmehealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit questions — SOC 2 / pen test window

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Legal and InfoSec reviewed the draft MSA + Order Form and had a few questions specifically on the security exhibit and audit language before we move to counters. Can you confirm the following?

1) SOC 2: do you have a recent SOC 2 report and a short summary we can share with our InfoSec team? Will you accept an NDA-first review or do you require an executed agreement?

2) Pen test / inspection: our policy requires a 30-day notice window for external penetration testing and a staging environment with read-only sample data. Can you confirm your pen-test notice and environment carveouts?

3) Audit rights & evidence cadence: we’d like a regular evidence cadence (quarterly or on-request with 5 business days SLA for shared artifacts). Is that consistent with Redwood’s operating model?

Attached our standard scoping form to capture dates and IP ranges. We can be flexible on sequencing if Redwood needs to route requests through legal first.

Can you please loop in whoever owns the security exhibit redlines on your side and propose a timeline for the legal review? Our procurement lead would like to keep this in the week of Sep 21 if possible.

Thanks,
Marta Diaz
Senior Counsel — Acme Health
[Attachment: PenTest_Scoping_Form.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Marta Diaz <marta.diaz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions — SOC 2 / pen test window

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karithk (legal) and Soojin (assurance) to confirm specifics. Quick answers up front:

- SOC 2: we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary immediately and provide the full SOC 2 under NDA/executed order form. I attached a short SOC2_report_summary.pdf for initial review.

- Pen test: Redwood requires a 14–60 day scheduling window depending on environment; for external prod-facing tests we ask for 30 days notice and a scoped staging lane for active testing. We will not allow tests against tenant production unless there is an explicit carveout and coordination with our ops team.

- Evidence cadence: we typically offer quarterly evidence bundles for active customers and ad-hoc artifact requests with a 5–7 business day turnaround for standard items (logs, network diagrams, controls mapping). For higher-sensitivity requests we escalate to the legal queue, which can add 3–5 business days.

Next steps I propose:
- Karithk and Soojin to propose specific redline language for the Order Form exhibit (pen-test language, notice period, scope) by EOD Sep 11.
- Acme to complete the attached PenTest_Scoping_Form with preferred windows and IPs.
- We’ll attach the proposed redlines to the MSA/Order Form and push to DocuSign if both sides agree.

Attachments: Proposed_MSARedlines_v1.pdf, SOC2_report_summary.pdf

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_MSARedlines_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, Marta Diaz <marta.diaz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions — SOC 2 / pen test window

Thanks Rachel / Marta — quick legal suggestions below based on Acme’s asks and our standard posture. I’m putting language you can paste into the security exhibit: 

1) Penetration testing / notice
- "Customer may conduct external penetration tests against Redwood environments with a minimum of thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Redwood. Customer shall use the PenTest_Scoping_Form to provide testing dates, IP ranges, tools to be used, and contact points. Redwood may require testing to occur in a segregated staging environment using synthetic or redacted data. Testing against multi-tenant production is prohibited unless expressly agreed in writing and executed by both parties."

2) SOC 2 / report access
- "Redwood will provide Customer a SOC 2 Type II summary at any time. Customer may request access to the full SOC 2 report subject to a mutually executed non-disclosure agreement and reasonable administrative process."

3) Evidence cadence & audit rights
- "Redwood will provide quarterly evidence bundles and will respond to ad-hoc evidence requests within five (5) business days for standard artifacts. For requests that require third-party attestations or broad operational access, Redwood may route requests through its legal and operations teams; such routing may extend response timelines by up to five (5) additional business days. Any inspection or forensic access will be subject to mutually agreed scheduling and scope limitations."

Notes: we should reconcile "audit rights" with procurement’s requested SLA for artifacts. If Acme needs guaranteed 5 business day turnaround for everything, we should propose a carveout in the Order Form (premium support / dedicated evidence lane).

I’ll mark these as tracked redlines and produce a clean .pdf for the Order Form. Rachel — if you’re comfortable, I’ll add an escalation path clause for SLA exceptions (legal review within 3 business days for redlines requiring immediate decision).

Karthik Iyer
Associate General Counsel
[Internal: please treat Proposed_MSARedlines_v1.pdf as draft]
